text: Raw data is sitting in Snowflake exactly as last night's extraction landed it. This video builds the first real dbt layer on top of it: one staging model per raw table.

The rule here is deliberately narrow. Rename and cast only -- no joins, no filters, no judgment calls -- and every model reads from a declared source, not a hardcoded table name, so dbt's lineage graph stays accurate.
stg_memberships takes the raw status-history rows and standardizes them -- consistent column names, real dates, a trimmed and uppercased status code -- without deciding what any of it means yet.
Generic tests catch basic data hygiene now: uniqueness, nulls, a closed set of status values. The test that checks Brightleaf's actual business rule comes in a later video.
Staging is clean and reconciled against the raw tables. Next: the one model that finally defines what 'active member' actually means.
